name: You Didn't Choose The Image; It's Deciding For You
description: Join us for a lecture that asks a deceptively simple question: who actually gets to decide what a hero, a victim, or a good life looks like?About the LectureWe don't choose the images that come to define us, and yet they decide more than we realise. A single gaze on a movie poster decides who counts as a hero. A familiar narrative arc decides who counts as a believable victim. A curated feed decides what a good life is supposed to look like.This talk moves through three of the speaker's own published studies — on Malayalam movie poster semiotics, on how Bollywood narratives construct the "ideal" rape victim, and on Instagram, loneliness, and FoMO among young Indians — to trace one quiet mechanism running underneath very different parts of Indian media. By the end, the question isn't really about posters, films, or apps. It's about who gets to build the image in the first place, and what we do with the gap between it and our own lives.About the SpeakerLydia Glory Jose is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Media and Journalism at IILM University, Gurugram, where she teaches media studies, visual communication, and research methods. Before academia, she worked as a journalist with Malayala Manorama, an experience that continues to shape how she reads Indian media — from the inside, not as an outsider looking in. Her research sits at the intersection of representation, visual semiotics, and digital media, published in Springer Nature's Sexuality and Culture, Palabra Clave, and the International Journal of Semiotics and Visual Rhetoric, and cited by the Times of India. Multilingual in Malayalam, Hindi, English, and Arabic, she remains, at heart, more interested in what an image is doing to us than in what it appears to be showing us.PS: Your Ticket Includes a 250/- Coupon Redeemable on F&BAbout unLectureunLecture brings experts out of classrooms and into cafés, bars and neighbourhood spaces across Delhi. Created by three friends from St. Stephen's, Delhi who wanted learning to feel warm, social and alive. Each event is an invitation to spend an evening with an idea.

description: Table for Ten: The Heirloom EditionTable for Ten is an intimate, 7-course, shared experience built around a simple idea: food is never just food. name: Blood on the Clocktower
description: ​During a hellish thunderstorm, a scream echoes through the sleepy town of Ravenswood Bluff. The townsfolk rush to investigate and find the beloved local storyteller has been murdered, their body hanging limp from the clocktower. As blood drips onto the cobblestones below, a realisation slowly dawns… a demon has been unleashed, killing by night and taking on human form by day. Can good find the demon in time? Or will evil overrun this once peaceful town?What is BotC?​Blood on the Clocktower is a game of murder and mystery, lies and logic, deduction and deception for five-to-twenty courageous players and one devious storyteller.​A social game played in person, seated in a circle, each player receives either a ‘good’ or ‘evil’ token with their unique character on it. Good players share information to solve the mystery whilst evil players lie about who they are and what they know. The good team wins if they can piece together their knowledge, trust each other, and execute the demon. The evil team wins if the demon can sow distrust, evade detection, and wipe out the town.

description: Adapting Alone: How Young People Are Redesigning Their Lives Around Climate ChangeClimate change doesn't always announce itself through a heatwave or a flood.More often, it reshapes the everyday. Taking an auto because waiting at a bus stop without shade feels unbearable.While we’ve accepted these adaptations as normal, they reveal a striking fact: young people are constantly adapting to a changing climate, often with little support from the institutions around them.Based on conversations with over 3,000 young people across 60 neighbourhoods in India, Mudito's latest research asks a simple but urgent question: Why has adapting to climate change become an individual responsibility?Join us for a conversation with incredible panelists as we explore the invisible work of adaptation, who is left to do it alone, and what it would take for our institutions to catch up.Date: August 7, 2026Time: 7 PM - 8 PM

name: Kalighat Painting with delectable Bengali Food
description: Step into the vibrant world of 19th-century Bengal through an immersive cultural experience that brings together art, storytelling, music, and food. This guided Kalighat painting workshop is led by acclaimed folk artists Sushama Chitrakar and Sanjay Chitrakar, who have devoted over 25 years to preserving and practising this iconic art form. Nationally recognised for their work, their paintings have been exhibited across India, making this a rare opportunity to learn directly from master artisans. The session begins with a live demonstration of the Kalighat painting process: from traditional colour mixing and the fundamentals of drawing to brushwork and composition. Along the way, the artists will share the folk songs traditionally sung while creating these paintings, as well as the stories, social commentary, and mythology that have long been depicted through this distinctive style.To complement the artistic journey, the experience features thoughtfully curated Bengali snack pairings inspired by the culinary traditions of the era, creating a sensory exploration of Bengal's rich cultural heritage. Guests will also have the opportunity to browse and purchase original Kalighat paintings created by the artists, offering a chance to take home an authentic piece of this living tradition.Whether you're an art enthusiast, a culture lover, or simply looking for a unique afternoon experience, this workshop offers an intimate introduction to one of India's most celebrated folk art traditions.Meet Your HostHi, I'm Shramana, a marketing professional born in Kolkata, now based in Delhi, with a deep love for India's art and food traditions. I started curating these experiences to make age-old crafts more accessible to the art-curious while creating meaningful opportunities for master artisans to share their knowledge. I believe cultural heritage thrives when it's experienced. Through intimate workshops, I hope to build a community that celebrates traditional arts, supports artisan livelihoods, and carries these legacies forward together.

description: In Odisha, Jalakhya is more than a word for snacks. Hosted at a private residence, Jalakhya is designed to feel less like a restaurant meal and more like being welcomed into an Odia home for an evening of food, conversation and togetherness.The experience begins with a guguni salad & crunchy Berhampur papad, alongside chilled fresh coconut water.From there, the table moves through crisp, tangy gup-chup and a generous chop basket. Guests can choose between chicken and mutton chops or vegetarian versions made with nadia aloo and kancha kadali, served with ambula rai dip. This course is paired with cooling tanka torani.No Odia snack table would be complete without dahi bara aloo dum—soft baras soaked in spiced curd and served with warm, comforting aloo dum.The next course reimagines a heartier Odia favourite: a mini whole-wheat roti folded around either boneless mutton kassa or mushroom kassa, with fresh salad and garlic hung curd. Think of it as an Odia-style mini taco, paired with a bright and refreshing ambula fizz.The evening ends on a sweet note with creamy coconut ice cream, crisp mini khaja, and a cup of aromatic Koraput coffee.What makes Jalakhya special is not only the food, but the way it is meant to be enjoyed—slowly, together, and with plenty of conversation. This is a table inspired by childhood evenings, neighbourhood favourites, roadside stalls, family recipes and the simple joy of sharing snacks with people you love.Come hungry. Stay for the stories.Please note: This is a seated set-menu experience hosted at a private residence. The complete menu will be served to all guests, with vegetarian and non-vegetarian options available for select courses. The menu is tentative and may change slightly depending on seasonality and ingredient availability.

name: In Search Of Djinns : Kotla Feroz Shah Walk
description: The walk takes you inside the fort of the 14th century ruler Firoz Shah Tughlaq built for his new capital Firozabad. The Kushak-e- Firoz (the Palace of Firoz) was strategically built at the banks of River Yamuna. The fort faced riverfront and lush green plains, its staircase leading you to the banks. It has a functioning mosque, a circular baoli (stepwell) known to have water snakes and a hypnotic effect on its visitors (it has recently been barricaded). The fort also has the magnificent Ashokan Pillar in Pali text erected at a height. It is confounding to any visitor how almost 27 tonne of heavy weighing monolith pillar was taken from Haryana and planted inside the fort at such a great height!Every Thursday evening Djinn (supernatural creatures in Islamic mythology) worship is performed in the complex, with visitors leaving their wish list, and a thread tied to the lattice for the Djinns to fulfill their wishes! The fort in recent years has gained the reputation of being haunted, because of the strong belief of Djinns inhabiting the fort.

name: Safdarjung Tomb Night Heritage Walk
description: Safdarjung’s Tomb Heritage Walkcurated by Darwesh heritage walks in collaboration with Sabhyata Foundation.Join us for a journey into the fading glow of Mughal splendour at Safdarjung's Tomb — often called the *last flicker of Mughal grandeur* in Delhi.Built in 1754 for Safdarjung, the powerful Nawab of Awadh and Prime Minister of the Mughal court, this monument stands at the twilight of an empire — grand in ambition, yet carrying within it the quiet signs of decline.Its story is as fascinating as its form. From courtly intrigues and shifting loyalties to the architectural choices that reveal a changing political landscape, Safdarjung’s life opens a compelling window into 18th-century Delhi.We will also trace a lesser-known layer of its history — how this tomb was constructed by reusing material from a pre-existing Mughal structure, quite literally building one memory over another.To truly understand Delhi — its rise, its resilience, and its gradual transitions — a visit to Safdarjung’s Tomb is essential.Come, walk with us through the final chapter of Mughal architectural brilliance — where grandeur meets gravity, and history lingers in every arch.

Hope to see you there!

name: Raat ke Afsane : Safdarjung Tomb
description: Safdarjung Tomb Walk: Stories After SunsetA guided heritage walk through the Safdarjung Tomb complex exploring the history, architecture and cultural significance of one of the last grand monuments of the Mughal era in Delhi.The walk highlights the transition from late Mughal power to emerging regional influences and explores the political, cultural and artistic context in which the monument was built. Participants will learn about its architecture, design elements and historical importance in Delhi’s heritage landscape.The experience is conducted during the evening, allowing participants to view the monument in a calm and atmospheric setting while engaging with its history through guided storytelling.Language of communication is Hindi and English.

name: The Procrastireaders
description: OverviewA slow reading circle designed around comfort, not pressure.This chapter of Procrastireaders steps out of the pages and into the scene of the crime, solving instead of just reading. You'll get a floor plan, real evidence cards, and secrets that only come out clue by clue, so the story unfolds the way a good twist should. Come with your sharpest theories and your best poker face, because this time the ending is in your hands, not the author's.What is Stories of Hope?We are a community led initiative dedicated to creating safe and mindful spaces. Through intimate workshops and gatherings, we help individuals navigate life's complexities from mental well being to personal growth with empathy and shared human connection.What to ExpectThe Concept: A relaxed, nostalgia filled session for anyone who has ever reread the series or wished their birthday came with an owl. Come as you are, no wands required.The Activities: Quizzes, house sorting conversations, favourite character debates, and a little friendly chaos over who really deserved Hermione.Shared Stories: We will talk about which book hit hardest, which character we related to most, and how the series shaped the way many of us fell in love with reading in the first place.Low Stakes: No pressure to have read every book seven times. Whether you are a die hard Potterhead or someone who just watched the movies, everyone is welcome at the table.Details🗓️ Date: 29th August (Saturday)⏰ Time: 11:30 AM📍 Location: Unlocked, 32nd Avenue☕ Inclusion: Coffee included🎟️ Fee: ₹700

name: A Night Heritage walk :  Humayun's Tomb & Museum
description: Step into the grandeur of Humayun's Tomb with us for an immersive Night heritage walk that goes beyond stone and symmetry.Curated by Darwesh Heritage Walks in collaboration with Sabhyata Foundation.We will not only explore the monument’s magnificent architecture, its Persian influences, and its place in the evolution of Mughal design — but also rediscover Humayun himself, perhaps the most underestimated of the Mughals. His struggles, exile, return, and legacy shaped the empire in ways we rarely pause to notice."Driven from his throne, yet never from his destiny's embrace,Humayun's return laid the path on which Akbar would leave his trace"Our journey will then continue to the Humayun's Tomb Museum — because no visit to the tomb is truly complete without experiencing the stories, artefacts, and narratives preserved there.Come, walk through history — and meet the emperor behind the monument.

name: Bazar-i-Husn :  exploring Tawaif culture
description: Step into the world of grace, wit, and artistry as we explore the lives of Tawaifs—the courtesans who once defined high culture, poetry, and performance in Delhi. This walk takes you through old city lanes that once echoed with ghazals, thumris, and the quiet power of women who shaped taste and tradition.Uncover the layered stories of kothas—not as places of shame, but as salons of sophistication, resistance, and refined art. Let’s reclaim these narratives and see history through a different lens.

name: Overthinkers Anonymous - Relationships Edition
description: Overthinkers Anonymous (Relationships Editions)OverviewA space for the relationships you carry but rarely talk about. People gather to finally say the things they've held back from a parent, a partner, a coworker, an in-law, anyone they can't avoid and can't quite be honest with. Said out loud, finally.Most relationship conflicts are not just about what happened; they are about how we interpret what happened. This session focuses on exploring how our thoughts shape our connections and why friction often feels more intense than the situation warrants. "Before You Blame" is a reflective workshop designed to help you look at your assumptions and inner patterns, moving you from reactivity toward steadiness and emotional responsibility.What is Stories of Hope?We are a community-led initiative dedicated to creating safe and mindful spaces. Through intimate workshops and gatherings, we help individuals navigate life’s complexities, from mental well-being to personal growth, with empathy and shared human connection.What to ExpectPattern Recognition: Explore how common emotional triggers and ego-driven patterns shape conflicts in marriage, family, or work.Internal Focus: Instead of trying to fix others, we gently shift the focus inward to understand our own interpretations and responses.Practical Tools: Learn actionable ways to question stressful thoughts and practice perspective shifts using real-life scenarios.Safe Exploration: A supportive, non-judgmental environment for honest discussion. This is a space for learning and reflection, not a lecture or therapy.Key TakeawaysClarity: Gain a deeper understanding of recurring relationship dynamics.Responsiveness: Walk away with tools to help you respond thoughtfully instead of reacting impulsively.Emotional Ownership: Build the internal steadiness needed to navigate life without requiring others to change first.Details🗓️ Date: 30th August (Sunday)⏰ Time: 11:30 AM📍 Location: Joaah Cafe

name: Shaam-e-Qutub :  Evening heritage walk
description: We are delighted to invite you to a special *evening heritage walk at Qutub Minar*, curated by Darwesh Heritage Walks in collaboration with Sabhyata Foundation.Experience the magic of one of Delhi’s most iconic monuments as it transforms at dusk—when the Qutub Minar complex is beautifully lit and wrapped in an almost timeless charm.This walk takes you through the story of Delhi’s first capital at Mehrauli, tracing the rise of the Tomars and Chauhans, and the arrival of the Delhi Sultanate under the early Turko-Afghan rulers. As the evening sets in, the illuminated ruins, soaring minar, and intricate carvings create a truly immersive atmosphere—perfect for experiencing history not just as a narrative, but as a living, breathing space.During this walk, we will explore:* The origins of Delhi’s earliest city at Mehrauli* The political transitions from Rajput to Sultanate rule* The architectural brilliance of the Qutub complex and its symbolism* The stories hidden in its mosque, pillars, and inscriptionsJoin us for an unforgettable evening of storytelling, history, and exploration—where the past comes alive under the soft glow of lights.We look forward to having you with us.(Please note: the fee is not for access to the site, but rather for curation of this experience)(Doesn't include monument entry ticket)
